entities.summary: Maria Corti was an Italian philologist, literary critic, and novelist. Considered one of the leading literary scholars of post-World War II Italy, she was awarded numerous prizes including the Premio Campiello for the entire body of her work. Her works of fiction were informed by her literary scholarship but also had a distinctly autobiographical vein, particularly her Voci del nord-est (1986) and II canto delle sirene (1989). For most of her career she was based at the University of Pavia where she established the Fondo Manoscritti di Autori Moderni e Contemporanei, an extensive curated archive of material on modern Italian writers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Maria Corti's literary scholarship and novel writing had a significant impact on Italian literature of post-World War II era, influencing generations of writers and scholars. Her work also contributed to the establishment of the University of Pavia's archive of modern Italian writers.
